Every structure named on this website is explained here in plain language, in Arabic and English.

The HAYKALAH Knowledge Center explains the terms used across this website: the Islamic finance contracts behind Sukuk and bank facilities, the vehicles that hold assets, the land and real-estate terms, the steps of HAYKALAH’s method, two Saudi laws, and the six ways HAYKALAH creates value. Each term has its own page in Arabic and English.

How the glossary works

  • One sentence first. Each term opens with a one-sentence definition.

  • Then a plain explanation of how the term works, in two or three short paragraphs.

  • How HAYKALAH uses it. Where the term appears in HAYKALAH’s work, with links to the pages and cases that cite it. Cases stay anonymized, and every figure carries its caption.

  • Related terms and pages to follow the idea further.

  • Two languages, one truth. The Arabic and English pages say the same thing.

  • General information only. The definitions describe concepts. They are not legal, Shariah or investment advice. Islamic finance terms are subject to Shariah review, and terms about laws and regulated activities to counsel review.

Islamic finance instruments

The Shariah contracts that Sukuk, funds and bank facilities are built on.

  • Sukukالصكوك Sukuk are Shariah-compliant certificates that represent an undivided share in an underlying asset, project or business activity, or in its returns.
  • Ijaraالإجارة Ijara is a Shariah-compliant lease in which the owner of an asset lets another party use it for an agreed term in return for an agreed rent.
  • Istisna’aالاستصناع Istisna’a is a Shariah-compliant contract to manufacture or build a specified asset for an agreed price, with delivery at a future date.
  • Murabahaالمرابحة Murabaha is a Shariah-compliant sale in which the seller discloses what an asset cost and sells it at that cost plus an agreed profit, often with payment deferred.
  • Musharakaالمشاركة Musharaka is a Shariah-compliant partnership in which two or more parties contribute capital to a venture, share its profit as agreed and bear its losses in proportion to their capital.
  • Wakalaالوكالة Wakala is a Shariah-compliant agency contract in which one party, the principal, appoints another, the agent or wakil, to act on its behalf, usually for an agreed fee.

Vehicles and structures

The companies, funds and endowments that hold assets, and the ways assets are turned into securities.

  • JV SPVشركة المشروع المشترك ذات الغرض الخاص A JV SPV is a company that two or more partners form for a single project or asset, so that the project’s ownership, finance and risk sit apart from the partners’ other businesses.
  • DevCo / ProjectCoشركة التطوير وشركة المشروع A DevCo/ProjectCo structure pairs one permanent development company, which holds a consortium’s origination, studies and know-how, with a separate project company formed for each tender or project.
  • Holding companyالشركة القابضة A holding company is a company whose main purpose is to own shares in other companies, so that ownership and control sit above the operating businesses.
  • Real-estate fundالصندوق العقاري A real-estate fund is an investment fund that pools investors’ money to own, develop or finance real estate, under the terms set out in the fund’s documents.
  • Off-balance-sheet vehicleالوعاء خارج الميزانية العمومية An off-balance-sheet vehicle is a separate entity that holds assets, and often the financing behind them, outside the sponsor’s own balance sheet, where the accounting rules allow it.
  • Securitizationالتوريق Securitization turns a pool of income-producing assets or receivables into securities that investors can buy, with payments on those securities funded by the pool’s cash flows.
  • Tokenizationترميز الأصول Tokenization records rights in an asset, such as ownership or a share of its income, as digital tokens on a digital ledger.
  • Waqfالوقف A waqf is an Islamic endowment in which an owner dedicates an asset permanently so that its income goes to the beneficiaries named in the waqf deed.
  • Nazirالناظر The nazir is the person or body that administers a waqf, managing its assets, collecting its income and distributing it as the waqf deed requires.

Real estate and land

How land and buildings are put to work without always being sold.

  • Musatahaالمساطحة Musataha is a right to build on and use land owned by another party for an agreed term, while the landowner keeps title to the land.
  • In-kind contributionالحصة العينية An in-kind contribution is a non-cash asset, such as land, that a partner contributes to a company in exchange for shares, at an agreed valuation.
  • Concessionالامتياز A concession is a contract that gives a party the right to operate an asset or a service for a set term, in return for payments or a share of the revenue.
  • Revenue shareمشاركة الإيرادات A revenue share is an agreement under which a party receives an agreed percentage of the revenue an asset or business produces, instead of, or in addition to, a fixed fee or rent.
  • Capital recyclingتدوير رأس المال Capital recycling is releasing capital from an asset once it earns, through refinancing or a sale, and reinvesting that capital in the next asset.
  • Mashaerالمشاعر المقدسة The Mashaer are the Holy Sites of Mina, Muzdalifah and Arafat, east of Masjid al-Haram in Makkah, through which pilgrims move during Hajj.

Process and deliverables

The steps, documents and terms HAYKALAH uses to take a project from idea to capital.

  • Deliverable codesرموز المخرجات HAYKALAH’s deliverable codes are the short names for the steps of the deliverable chain it has reused for 22 years, from market research to due diligence, each of which answers one question.
  • Model of recordالنموذج المالي المعتمد A model of record is the single financial model that every party to a transaction agrees to use as the reference for its numbers.
  • Data roomغرفة البيانات A data room is a secure, organized store of the documents that investors and lenders review, holding one version of every document.
  • HOAMمصفوفة HOAM HOAM, the HAYKALAH Opportunity Assessment Matrix, is HAYKALAH’s tool for scoring a new opportunity on six axes and comparing it with two decades of precedent.
  • Equity-for-buildالحصة مقابل البناء Equity-for-build is a model in which HAYKALAH takes part of its reward as equity in the company or project it builds, vesting at agreed milestones, instead of fees alone.
  • Vestingالاستحقاق على مراحل Vesting is the process by which shares or other rights promised to a person become theirs in stages, as agreed conditions such as time or milestones are met.
  • Shareholders’ agreementاتفاقية الشركاء A shareholders’ agreement is a contract among a company’s shareholders that sets how the company is owned, governed and funded, and how shareholders can enter or leave.

Regulation and data

Two Saudi laws that shape how HAYKALAH’s work is structured and how this website handles data.

  • PDPLنظام حماية البيانات الشخصية The PDPL is the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law, which sets how personal data may be collected, used, shared and kept, and is overseen by the Saudi Data & AI Authority (SDAIA).
  • PSP Lawنظام التخصيص The PSP Law is the Saudi Private Sector Participation Law, which sets the rules for public-private partnerships and privatization in the Kingdom.

Six ways we create value

HAYKALAH’s six features: how we create value for clients.

  • Innovationالابتكار Innovation is the first of HAYKALAH’s six ways of creating value: designing the structure a deal needs, even when no template exists.
  • Monetizationتحقيق العائد Monetization is the second of HAYKALAH’s six ways of creating value: turning assets that cost money to hold into recurring income and capital.
  • Optimizationالتحسين Optimization is the third of HAYKALAH’s six ways of creating value: testing every option before capital is committed, then choosing the best use, cost and control.
  • Automationالأتمتة Automation is the fourth of HAYKALAH’s six ways of creating value: automating reporting, records and routine operations, so that people spend their time on judgment.
  • Transformationالتحوّل Transformation is the fifth of HAYKALAH’s six ways of creating value: changing how an organization, an asset or a portfolio works, from governance to data.
  • Commercializationالتسويق التجاري Commercialization is the sixth of HAYKALAH’s six ways of creating value: taking ideas, knowledge and public assets to market with a business model, an operator and paying users.

Questions

Is the glossary advice?

No. The glossary explains concepts in general terms. It is not legal, Shariah or investment advice, and it does not take account of any particular transaction.

Who checks the definitions?

Islamic finance definitions go to Shariah review, and definitions of laws and regulated activities to counsel, before they are final. These definitions are general explanations, not legal advice or a Shariah ruling.

Why are the cases anonymized?

HAYKALAH does not name clients until they consent in writing. Each case shows the year, the role, the status as recorded and the evidence grade instead.

Can I ask about a term that is not here?

Yes. Ask HAYKALAH (Beta) answers from HAYKALAH’s published pages, or you can write to haykalah@haykalah.com.

Ask about a structure, or tell us what you want to structure. We can start under an NDA.
